topic: Breath series 4b: Cyclic sighing, breathe-along short version (off grid)
caption:
Three slow cyclic sighs, paced for you: in through the nose, one short sniff, then a long breath out through the mouth.

Take a full, slow inhale through your nose. At the top, take one short, sharp sniff in to fully expand your lungs. Then breathe out in one long, slow exhale through your mouth. The Reel paces it at about three seconds in, one for the sniff and eight out, but go at your own pace.

If you feel light-headed, go back to your usual breathing. Research on this technique has excluded people with heart disease, glaucoma, a history of seizures or pregnancy, so check with your doctor first if any of these apply to you.

The short version of our cyclic sighing Reel. The full guided version, with the research behind it, is on our profile @equal_psychology.

Save this for another time.
